mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and stable for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar high-rate periods, or FEDFUNDS drops below 4% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as labor market weakness reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar labor weakening events, or wage growth (inferred from UNRATE) rises while employment falls.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (GDPC1) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals robust consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly > previous month AND > previous two months (3-month trend)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant over 100 similar 3-month demand expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as it indicates weakening manufacturing momentum and reduced earnings visibility.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of similar contractions (rolling 12-month window).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months in a tightening regime, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates a potential rate cut cycle.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 and stable for two months AND FEDFUNDS > 5.0 (tightening phase)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of similar pre-cut episodes (defined by UNRATE < 3.5 and FEDFUNDS > 5).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 jobs with no change in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests a strong labor market, predicting positive S&P 60-day forward returns via optimism about growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 AND UNRATE unchanged from previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 80% of analogous labor surge events (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% for two consecutive months in a stable economy predicts positive S&P 20-day forward returns as it reduces growth fears and supports equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 3.0 and stable for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of similar low-inflation episodes (rolling 6-month window).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining home prices (assumed proxy via HOUST) by more than 5% predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns as it signals housing market stress and reduced consumer wealth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar housing declines (measured by HOUST).
